inputs.userGoal: Right, it seems cloureflared and apisix are the most pressing matter (none are pressing, all these resources will be gone in 1month anyways as I finish the startup program). Do you want to start planning for deploying those 2? I have doppler for use as secrets unless key vault can manage
subGoals: Cost-optimized one-month pilot: avoid fixed-cost managed gateway services and use one small gateway VM.
Private-origin security: expose no public IP on the gateway VM; use Cloudflare Tunnel for ingress and NAT only for explicit egress.
Incremental brownfield integration: preserve existing Neo4j resources and use Azure Key Vault with managed identity for runtime secrets.
insightsApplied: insight-resource-13: Preserve the existing Neo4j operator SSH rule and add only narrow gateway-to-origin rules.
insight-resource-14: Reuse the existing Neo4j VNet and add connectivity rather than creating a duplicate workload VNet.
insight-resource-24: Use the existing vnet-ai-access edge VNet and its reserved snet-tunnel placement for the gateway.
insight-resource-92: Use the empty reserved snet-tunnel subnet for the private gateway and add only the approved subnet associations.
insight-resource-17: Use the existing RBAC-enabled Key Vault as the candidate runtime secret store without putting values in IaC.
insight-resource-12: Retain the existing Neo4j public IP as a break-glass path; never attach it to the new gateway.
insight-resource-20: Treat the existing Neo4j VM as the pilot origin for Registry and Keycloak.

resources.name: nsg-mcp-edge
resources.subtype: Private gateway subnet network security group

reasoning.whyChosen: A subnet-level NSG keeps the gateway private and denies unsolicited inbound traffic. Explicit outbound rules support Azure management, DNS, NTP, HTTPS package/API traffic, and Cloudflare QUIC while the peered Neo4j origin is reachable through the VirtualNetwork service tag.
alternativesConsidered: Reuse the existing Neo4j NSG, rejected because it would couple gateway and origin policy.
Allow the public Internet inbound and rely only on Cloudflare, rejected because a tunnel origin does not require inbound exposure.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The NSG remains a coarse subnet boundary; APISIX route policy and application authorization must enforce service-specific access. Cloudflare IP allowlisting is not used at the VM because tunnel traffic terminates locally.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The NSG must be associated with the existing tunnel subnet that hosts the new gateway VM.

resources.name: pip-mcp-edge-egress

properties.inboundBehavior: NAT Gateway does not accept unsolicited inbound connections

reasoning.whyChosen: A Standard static public IP is required by the Standard NAT Gateway and provides deterministic egress for the private gateway subnet. It is not attached to the VM NIC and cannot be used as an origin listener.
alternativesConsidered: A public IP on the VM NIC, rejected because it would create a directly addressable origin and management surface.
Implicit Azure outbound access, rejected for the pilot because the subnet should have an explicit, reviewable egress path.
reasoning.tradeoffs: This adds a small public-IP and NAT processing cost, but the address is egress-only and avoids exposing APISIX or SSH.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The public IP is consumed by the NAT Gateway rather than by the gateway VM.

resources.name: nat-mcp-edge-egress

reasoning.whyChosen: The gateway VM is intentionally placed in a private subnet. A Standard NAT Gateway gives cloudflared, Azure VM Agent, package updates, and controlled API calls a deterministic outbound path without allowing inbound DNAT.
alternativesConsidered: Implicit/default outbound access, rejected because it is not deterministic and is being retired for private-subnet designs.
Azure Firewall or a managed gateway, rejected as disproportionate fixed cost and complexity for a one-month single-VM pilot.
reasoning.tradeoffs: NAT Gateway is a fixed-cost component and does not provide egress filtering by destination domain; the NSG supplies port-level egress controls. The single gateway VM remains the availability bottleneck.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The NAT Gateway needs a Standard static public IP and is associated directly with the existing tunnel subnet.

resources.name: nic-mcp-edge

reasoning.whyChosen: A standalone private NIC makes the VM-to-subnet relationship explicit and prevents an accidental public IP association. Dynamic private allocation avoids reserving an address in the shared pilot subnet while the subnet NSG supplies the boundary policy.
alternativesConsidered: Static private IP, deferred until route automation requires a stable gateway address.
A public NIC, rejected because Cloudflare Tunnel is outbound-only.
reasoning.tradeoffs: A dynamic private address must be discovered from deployment output or Azure inventory when authoring APISIX management routes; the pilot's upstream origin address is the existing fixed Neo4j address.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The NIC must be created in the existing tunnel subnet and use the new subnet security policy.

resources.name: vm-mcp-edge

services: Apache APISIX in standalone declarative YAML mode
cloudflared as a system-managed outbound tunnel connector
bootstrap.secretSource: Existing Key Vault through the VM system-assigned identity after RBAC assignment propagation
bootstrap.adminApi: Disabled by default; if temporarily enabled, bind to loopback and require authentication
bootstrap.management: Optional Cloudflare Access SSH route to localhost:22; no public SSH listener

routes.purpose: Keycloak pilot route; switch the origin to production HTTPS before public exposure

reasoning.whyChosen: A small Linux VM is the lowest-complexity common origin-side control point for a Cloudflare Tunnel connector and APISIX across VM workloads. Standard_B2s provides two vCPUs and four GiB memory for the pilot's gateway, while Trusted Launch, SSH-key-only access, system identity, and no public IP provide a hardened baseline.
alternativesConsidered: Standard_B1ms, rejected because the live subscription SKU query reported a subscription restriction and its memory is marginal for Docker, APISIX, and cloudflared.
A second Container App or managed gateway, rejected because the current pilot origin is a VM and the user selected a low-cost private gateway.
APISIX with etcd and multiple replicas, deferred until durable state and HA are required.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The VM is a single point of failure and its exact B2s capacity must be rechecked at deployment time. The pinned Ubuntu image version is intentionally immutable and requires an explicit update when refreshed. Keycloak is currently a start-dev HTTP service on the origin and must be switched to a production configuration before treating the public route as production-ready.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The VM requires the private NIC and must be placed in the existing tunnel subnet; the Key Vault role assignment is applied after the VM creates its system identity.

references.title: Azure Linux VM SSH key authentication

resources.name: peer-ai-access-to-neo4j

reasoning.whyChosen: The edge and Neo4j address spaces are non-overlapping (10.50.0.0/16 and 10.42.0.0/16), so symmetric VNet peering gives APISIX private reachability to the existing Registry and Keycloak listeners without a public origin route.
alternativesConsidered: Public origin access through Cloudflare, rejected because the tunnel architecture is intended to remove inbound origin exposure.
VPN Gateway or Azure Virtual WAN, rejected as unnecessary fixed cost and operational complexity for two VNets.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Peering is regional and does not create transitive connectivity to the unrelated Langfuse or Container Apps networks. The origin NSG must still explicitly allow only the gateway subnet ports.

resources.dependencyReasoning: A peering is a child resource of the edge VNet and references the existing Neo4j VNet as its remote network.

resources.name: peer-neo4j-to-ai-access

reasoning.whyChosen: Azure VNet peering is configured as a pair. Creating the reverse peering makes the private route symmetric and allows return traffic from Registry and Keycloak to the APISIX gateway.
alternativesConsidered: One-sided peering, rejected because both directions are required for normal TCP request and response flows.
A route table or custom appliance route, rejected because the gateway is an application proxy, not a transit router.
reasoning.tradeoffs: This changes the existing Neo4j VNet topology and must be included in the Azure what-if review, but it does not recreate or resize the Neo4j VM.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The reverse peering is a child resource of the existing Neo4j VNet and references the existing edge VNet.

resources.name: ra-mcp-edge-kv-secrets-user

reasoning.whyChosen: The gateway needs to read only the Cloudflare tunnel token and APISIX/OIDC runtime secret material. Key Vault Secrets User is narrower than contributor or administrator roles and follows the existing vault's RBAC model.
alternativesConsidered: Reuse the existing Neo4j user-assigned identity, rejected because it couples two workloads and its attachment/scope is not the least-privilege default.
Doppler on the VM, retained only as an optional local/bootstrap source and rejected as the Azure runtime authority.
A Key Vault administrator role, rejected because the gateway does not need to create, rotate, purge, or manage vault objects.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Role-assignment propagation can lag VM creation, so bootstrap must retry without logging secret values. Secret objects are pre-seeded through a separate protected workflow; no secret value is stored in this plan.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The VM's system-assigned principal does not exist until the VM is created, and the role assignment is scoped to the existing Key Vault.

references.title: Azure RBAC role assignments with Bicep

reasoning.whyChosen: The existing edge VNet already contains the reserved tunnel subnet and is the approved placement for the new private gateway VM.
alternativesConsidered: Create a new hub VNet, deferred because it would add cost and migration work during a one-month pilot.
reasoning.tradeoffs: This VNet becomes the first edge spoke for the pilot; future Container Apps and Langfuse connectivity require separate network design.

resources.name: existing-edge-subnet
resources.subtype: Existing tunnel subnet with additive associations

reasoning.whyChosen: The subnet was reserved for the tunnel workload and has no current IP configurations, delegations, or service endpoints. Associating the new NSG, NAT Gateway, and Key Vault service endpoint wires the VM into the approved private edge boundary.
alternativesConsidered: Create a second subnet in vnet-ai-access, deferred because the existing reservation is sufficient for this pilot.
Leave default outbound access implicit, rejected in favor of an explicit NAT path.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Changing defaultOutboundAccess is a topology change and must be reviewed with what-if. The subnet remains sized for a small pilot, not a multi-replica gateway fleet.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The subnet update must reference the existing parent VNet and the new NSG and NAT Gateway associations.

references.title: Private subnets and default outbound access

reasoning.whyChosen: The existing Neo4j VNet contains the Registry and Keycloak pilot origin at private address 10.42.1.4. Its address space does not overlap the edge VNet, satisfying the peering constraint.
alternativesConsidered: Move Registry and Keycloak to a new workload VNet, deferred until the current VM workload is separated.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The VNet has overlapping address space with the Langfuse VNet, so this plan deliberately does not peer Langfuse.

resources.name: existing-neo4j-vm

requiredOriginConfigurationChanges: Bind only Registry HTTPS/HTTP and Keycloak's front-door listener to the VM private interface (or a deliberately protected all-interface binding); keep Neo4j, databases, OpenBao, monitoring, and admin ports loopback-only.
Configure APISIX upstream TLS/SNI and the reviewed internal CA for Registry HTTPS before enabling the route.
Switch Keycloak from start-dev/HTTP to its production start mode with the exact Cloudflare external hostname before public exposure.
Set the Registry and auth-server external URLs and exact OAuth redirect allowlist to the Cloudflare hostnames.
properties.retainedUntil: Cloudflare Access management and private origin validation complete

reasoning.whyChosen: The pilot fronts the already-verified Registry and Keycloak services on this VM rather than moving application state during the edge rollout.
alternativesConsidered: Deploy a second application VM, deferred because it would duplicate state and extend the one-month pilot.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The existing VM remains a combined Neo4j and Registry workload, and its public IP is retained as a break-glass path. The Registry and Keycloak listeners remain loopback-only until the origin-side configuration is changed to accept the peered gateway subnet.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The origin is reachable only after symmetric peering exists and the existing origin NSG has the two narrowly scoped gateway rules.

resources.name: existing-neo4j-nsg
resources.subtype: Existing origin NSG with additive gateway rules

reasoning.whyChosen: The current origin NSG permits only operator SSH. Adding rules for the gateway subnet and the exact transformed host ports allows APISIX to reach only the two approved pilot surfaces without opening Neo4j, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, OpenBao, or monitoring ports.
alternativesConsidered: Allow all traffic from the peered VNet, rejected because it would overgrant access to the origin VM.
Open the default Compose ports 80/443/8080, rejected because the verified Azure transformation uses host ports 18080/18443/18081.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The Keycloak rule is HTTP for the current start-dev canary and is not the final production posture; switch Keycloak to production mode and an authenticated TLS origin before public launch.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The rules use the edge subnet CIDR and are meaningful only after the two VNets are peered.

references.title: Azure network security group security rules

resources.name: existing-key-vault

reasoning.whyChosen: The existing vault already has RBAC, soft delete, purge protection, and a deny-by-default firewall. Adding the gateway subnet service endpoint lets the gateway identity retrieve only the pilot secrets without copying values into VM images, IaC, or Compose files.
alternativesConsidered: Doppler as the runtime authority, deferred to local/bootstrap use because Azure managed identity plus Key Vault is the native least-privilege path.
Create a new vault or private endpoint, deferred to avoid duplicating the existing protected vault during the pilot.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The vault's public network access setting remains enabled with a deny firewall and AzureServices bypass; a private endpoint is a later hardening step. Secret values and initial provisioning are intentionally outside this plan.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The vault network rule uses the edge subnet, and the gateway VM role assignment is scoped to this vault.

overallReasoning.summary: Add a private APISIX and cloudflared gateway VM to the existing rg-ai-access edge VNet, associate it with the reserved snet-tunnel subnet, and connect that VNet to the existing Neo4j VNet through symmetric peering. Cloudflare remains the public DNS, TLS, WAF, Access, and tunnel perimeter. APISIX runs in standalone declarative mode and routes only the Registry and Keycloak pilot hostnames to the existing Neo4j VM private address.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: The pilot uses one Standard_B2s VM, so the gateway is a single point of failure and is not an HA design. A Standard NAT Gateway and static Standard public IP add a small fixed monthly cost but provide deterministic outbound connectivity while keeping the VM private and preventing unsolicited inbound traffic. The existing Key Vault remains public-network-enabled with a deny firewall and service endpoint rather than gaining a new private endpoint. No new monitoring workspace, private DNS zone, Container Apps VNet integration, or etcd cluster is included in this one-month pilot. The existing Neo4j public IP and operator SSH rule are retained until Cloudflare Access management is independently validated. Cloudflare account resources and APISIX/cloudflared application configuration are external follow-up work, not Azure ARM resources. All other insight-resource entries in .azure/insights.json are retained unchanged because they are not dependencies of this Registry/Keycloak gateway pilot.
unappliedInsights: The existing user-assigned Neo4j identity is not reused because its VM attachment and scope are not the least-privilege default for a separate gateway.
The existing AI-access Container Apps remain out of scope because their environment is not VNet-integrated.
The overlapping Langfuse address space remains out of scope; it cannot be directly peered with the Neo4j VNet without redesign.

plan.validation: The resource graph is additive: new gateway resources are placed in rg-ai-access, existing VNets/subnets/NSG/VM/Key Vault are referenced by full ARM ID, and no existing resource is represented as a new resource. Before IaC generation, verify the B2s SKU at deployment time, confirm the 10.50.1.4 private address is available if a static NIC address is selected, and use Azure what-if to confirm only the intended creations and narrowly scoped existing-resource updates appear.
architecturePrinciples: Private origin with no gateway VM public IP
Cloudflare at the public edge and APISIX behind the tunnel
Incremental brownfield integration with no recreation
